A federal jury on Friday ordered Apple to pay more than $5.7 billion after finding that the vibration motors in several iPhone and Apple Watch models infringed patents owned by a small haptics technology company.

Apple said it would appeal. The company argued at trial that the patents were invalid and that its engineers had designed the motors independently years before the patents were filed.

The verdict is one of the largest patent awards against Apple, though large jury awards are often reduced or overturned on appeal. Shares of Apple were little changed in afternoon trading.
